sentences.text: S.B. Criminal Misc Suspension Of Sentence Application (Appeal)

In  S.B. Criminal Appeal No.2240/2022 Rajendra @ Babbal S/o Shri Ramjilal, Aged About 28 Years,
Resident Of Village Khatnawali, Police Station Bayana, Tehsil Bayana, District Bharatpur (Rajasthan) (Presently Confined In Sevar Jail, District Bharatpur)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through The Public Prosecutor ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Ms. Shweta Soni For Respondent(s) : Mr. Amit Punia, PP
For Complainant(s) : Mr. Anshul Sharma HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR UPMAN Order 08/10/2024 1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant-appellant, learned State Counsel as well as counsel for the complainant on the application for suspension of execution of sentence.

2. The applicant-appellant herein has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376(2)(i) of IPC and Section 5/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012 vide judgment dated 13.09.2022 passed by Presiding Officer, Special Court, Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 & Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, No.2, Bharatpur (Raj.) in Sessions Case No.39/2020 (54/2019) and has been sentenced to maximum punishment of ten years.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant-applicant submits that appellant-applicant has wrongly been convicted by the learned trial Court.
Counsel submits that learned trial Court has failed to appreciate the evidence available on record in correct perspective.
Counsel submits that initially when FIR was registered allegation of sexual intercourse was levelled against the appellant by the victim.
It is submitted that during the course of investigation, victim as well as witnesses changed their version and levelled allegation of oral sex against the appellant.
It is submitted that during the course of trial, victim changed her version again and levelled allegation of sexual intercourse against the appellant.

It is submitted that there is no medical corroboration of the allegations levelled by the Rajendra @ Babbal S/O Shri Ramjilal vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jp:42275) on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151300141/
1 victim as no sign of sexual assault was found on the person of the victim who is aged about 7 years.
Counsel submits that medical expert specifically stated that he did not find any sign of sexual assault on the person of the victim.

It is submitted that there is money dispute between the appellant and brother of the complainant and same is evident from the fact that proceedings under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act is going on between the parties.

Counsel submits that the fact about money dispute between the parties is also evident from the statements of PW-1 and PW-2, who were independent witnesses produced by the prosecution and it appears from their testimony that on the date of alleged incident, heated arguments took place between appellant and grand-father of the victim on account of money dispute.
Counsel submits that during trial appellant was on bail and he did not misuse the liberty of bail.

It is submitted that [2024:RJ-JP:42275] (3 of 5)
[SOSA-1460/2022] offences under Section 3(1)(w)(i) & 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act were not proved against the appellant during the course of trial.

Counsel further submits that appellant has suffered incarceration of about two years and eleven months including remission and there is no immediate prospect of this appeal being heard and disposed of in near future.
4.
Learned State counsel assisted by counsel for the complainant vehemently opposes the submissions made by counsel for the appellant.
They submit that there is specific allegation against the appellant of commission of oral sex upon the victim who is aged about seven years.

5. Upon a consideration of the arguments advanced on behalf of counsel for the appellant, learned State Counsel as well as counsel for the complainant and having regard to the facts and circumstances as available on the record and especially the fact that there is no medical corroboration of the allegations levelled by the victim; inconsistency in the statement of victim as well as witnesses at different stages and so also considering the fact that there was money dispute between the parties and further considering the period of incarceration suffered by the appellant

,
this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has available to him strong grounds to assail the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence.
Thus, it is a fit case for suspending the sentences awarded to the applicant-appellant during pendency of the instant appeal.

Accordingly, the application for suspension of sentence filed under Section 389 of Cr.PC is allowed and it is ordered that the sentences passed by the Presiding Officer, Special Court,
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 & Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, No.2, Bharatpur (Raj.) vide judgment dated 13.09.2022 in Sessions Case No.39/2020 (54/2019) against the appellant-applicant Rajendra @ Babbal S/o Shri Ramjilal shall remain suspended till final disposal of the aforesaid appeal and he shall be released on bail, provided he execute a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance in this court on 08.11.2024 and whenever ordered to do so till the disposal of the appeal on the conditions indicated below:-
1. That he will appear before the trial Court in the month of January of every year till the appeal is decided.
